subject: [PATCH v3 0/4] mm: read root memcg stats from global counters instead of flushing

reviews.author: Chris Down
reviews.summary: Reviewer Chris Down noted that the patch improves performance for workloads in the root cgroup under memory pressure, and provided Reviewed-by and Tested-by tags.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Joanne,

Thanks, I've reproduced this and the results are definitely much better now,
in that with this patch it now writes back pages for a workload in the root
cgroup under memory pressure.

Reviewed-by: Chris Down <chris@chrisdown.name>
Tested-by: Chris Down <chris@chrisdown.name>

Thanks!

Chris

reviews.author: Chris Down
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Chris Down noted that the patch does not handle the case where the root memcg is being scanned, and requested a fix to ensure that global counters are used instead of flushing in this scenario.

Reviewer Chris Down pointed out that the patch description still refers to a denylist, which was changed to an allowlist in v2, and requested that the changelog be updated to explicitly list the stats that only change through mod_lruvec_state()

Reviewer noted that NR_VMSCAN_WRITE is not on the exclusion list and would cause a mix of live node counter and stale rstat value in root reclaim, requesting it be added to the exclusion list.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Joanne,

Joanne Koong writes:

---

This still describes the v2 denylist. With the allowlist, the root memcg
also keeps reading rstat for NR_ANON_MAPPED, NR_FILE_MAPPED, NR_SHMEM et
al, and some of those differ for reasons outside the two categories here,
like swapcache being counted differently in the node counter, for
example. Could the changelog say what is on the list instead? So that
would be the stats that only change through mod_lruvec_state(), with
everything else still reading rstat.

---

NR_VMSCAN_WRITE isn't on the list, but prepare_scan_control() adds it to
WORKINGSET_RESTORE_ANON, so once the root flush in reclaim goes away,
root reclaim would mix a live node counter with a stale rstat value.
Unless I'm mistaken it should go here as well.

Once those are fixed, please feel free to add:

Reviewed-by: Chris Down <chris@chrisdown.name>

Thanks!

Chris

reviews.author: Chris Down
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Chris Down noted that the patch does not handle the case where the root memcg's stats are being read by count_shadow_nodes() and filemap_cachestat(), which require local or arbitrary memcg stats, respectively.

Reviewer Chris Down suggested implementing a mem_cgroup_flush_lru_stats_ratelimited() helper to simplify the root check in memcontrol.c, but stated that it's not necessary to hold up this patch and confirmed that refaults in the root cgroup no longer flush.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Joanne,

Joanne Koong writes:

---

Not a big deal, but in the v2 thread you mentioned you would try a
mem_cgroup_flush_lru_stats_ratelimited() helper for this, per Michal's
suggestion. That still seems like a good idea given this skip and the one in
DAMON rely on everything read after them staying in lruvec_use_node_stat(),
and at least speaking for myself, keeping the root check close to the list
in memcontrol.c makes that easier to see. It doesn't need
to hold this patch up though, and I've tested that refaults in the root
cgroup no longer flush, so either way:

Reviewed-by: Chris Down <chris@chrisdown.name>
Tested-by: Chris Down <chris@chrisdown.name>

Thanks!

Chris

reviews.author: Chris Down
reviews.summary: Reviewer Chris Down confirmed that the patch works as intended and provided Reviewed-by and Tested-by tags, indicating a positive review.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Joanne,

I've tested that this works well.

Reviewed-by: Chris Down <chris@chrisdown.name>
Tested-by: Chris Down <chris@chrisdown.name>

Thanks!

Chris

2026-11-16.patch_summary: This patch series modifies the Linux kernel to read memory cgroup (memcg) statistics from global counters instead of flushing them, which is expensive and can lead to stale stats. The root memcg's stats are updated directly from global counters, eliminating the need for flushing in most cases. However, three remaining flushes will be addressed in a subsequent patchset. This change improves performance by reducing the time it takes to read memcg statistics, especially on systems with many CPUs and active memory allocation.

reviews.author: Joanne Koong (author)
reviews.summary:
Author acknowledged that the root memcg's stats should include accounted kernel memory allocated by tasks in the root cgroup, but stated that addressing this is left for a separate subsequent patchset.

Author acknowledges that the analysis is correct and agrees to add NR_VMSCAN_WRITE to the allowlist, also plans to investigate adding more stats to the allowlist as suggested by Sashiko.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Chris,

Thanks for reviewing and testing this series!

---

I think your analysis is right. I'll add NR_VMSCAN_WRITE to the allow
list as well.

Sashiko pointed out that NR_SWAPCACHE and the other charged-folio
stats between WORKINGSET_RESTORE_FILE and
PGPROMOTE_SUCCESS in memcg_node_stat_items[] also should be added as
well. I need to look into this more.

I'm out on PTO for three weeks but when I come back, I'll update this
series and submit v4.

Thanks,
Joanne

reviews.author: Joanne Koong (author)
reviews.summary:
Author acknowledged that the root memcg's stats should include accounted kernel memory allocated by tasks in the root cgroup, and agreed to address this in a separate subsequent patchset.

The author is addressing Chris Down's feedback about adding a helper function for ratelimited flushes and non-ratelimited flushes, which Joanne found to be overkill after testing. Instead of implementing the helper, she suggests adding comments at the callsites and above lruvec_use_node_stat() to document the dependency.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Chris,

On Mon, Nov 16, 2026 at 9:07 PM Chris Down <chris@chrisdown.name> wrote:

---

Thanks for reviewing and testing this series. When I was updating v2
-> v3, I tested out what adding the helper looks like, but found it a
bit overkill. It adds two new api wrappers (one for ratelimited
flushes for workingset, and one for non-ratelimited flushes for
damon), each of which has only one callsite.

Maybe it would be clearest to add a comment directly at the callsites
and above lruvec_use_node_stat() to document the dependency? I'm happy
to add this in, or if you and Michal prefer the helper still, I'm
happy to add the helper APIs.

Thanks,
Joanne
